title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Templates and SOPs
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards, templates, and runnable runbooks. It is intended for engineers, SREs, incident commanders (ICs), and on-call responders. Use these templates to: declare incidents, run playbooks, notify customers, and produce consistent postmortems and follow-ups.

Scope

- Services covered: public API, serving runtime, orchestration/control plane, logging/observability, dedicated customer pools, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem).
- This document covers: incident lifecycle, severity definitions, runbook and run-step templates, on-call rotations and handoffs, game days, status page messages, customer comms templates, and postmortem process.

Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): leads the incident, owns the incident timeline, and ensures communication.
- Primary On-Call (Primary): first responder for the service; executes runbooks and escalates.
- Secondary On-Call (Secondary): backup responder and deep-troubleshooter.
- Triage/Responder: engineers pulled in for specific subsystems.
- Communications Lead: owns status page updates and external customer comms.
- Postmortem Owner: leads RCA and follow-up tracking.

Severity definitions and SLAs

1) Sev 1 (P0) — Critical outage
- Customer impact: major outage for key endpoints (e.g., API returns 5xx, serving runtime unavailable).
- Business impact: large portion of customers affected or revenue impact.
- SLOs: Restore service (user-visible) within 60 minutes target, mitigate within 15 minutes (initial rollback/fallback).
- PagerDuty: page Primary -> Secondary -> IC -> Eng Manager.

2) Sev 2 (P1) — Degraded but functional
- Customer impact: high latency, partial feature loss, increased error rate but partial service available.
- SLOs: Detect and start mitigation in 30 minutes, full resolution within 8 hours.
- PagerDuty: page Primary; escalate to Secondary after 30 minutes if unresolved.

3) Sev 3 (P2) — Non-urgent but high visibility
- Customer impact: minor regressions, single-customer or non-critical paths.
- SLOs: Triage within 4 business hours, resolution within 3 business days.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1) Detection
- Source: alerts (Prometheus, Datadog), customer reports, internal dashboards, or automated SLO monitors.
- Initial action: acknowledge alert in PagerDuty, add short summary in incident channel: "[IC] Acknowledged alert — initial hypothesis".

2) Declaration
- If customer impact matches Sev 1/2 definitions, declare incident in our incident channel (#incidents) and create an incident thread in the incident tracker (Jira/Confluence incident pages).
- Assign an IC.

3) Triage
- IC confirms severity, assigns responders, and posts the first update: summary, scope, timeline, owner, and initial mitigation steps.
- Start a dedicated incident Slack channel: #incident-<short-name>-<date>.

4) Mitigation & remediation
- Follow the service-specific runbook. If no runbook exists, follow the generic mitigation runbook below.
- Apply short-term mitigations (traffic split, circuit break, fallback to model-variant, scale up capacity).

5) Communication
- Internal: IC posts updates every 15 minutes for Sev 1 until mitigated, every 60 minutes for Sev 2. Use the incident channel and page updates.
- External: Communications Lead prepares status-page updates and customer messages per templates below.

6) Resolution & validation
- IC confirms resolution criteria met (SLO restored, traffic normalized, error rates back to baseline). Validate with metrics and smoke tests.

7) Post-incident
- Create or update the postmortem within 48 hours; initial draft by Postmortem Owner within 72 hours.
- Track action items (owner + due date) in the incident Jira ticket.

Generic mitigation runbook (template)

Use for services without a specialized runbook. Keep steps concise and actionable.

- Step 0: Safety first
  1. Acknowledge page in PagerDuty.
  2. Create incident channel and incident page.
  3. Assign IC and Communications Lead.

- Step 1: Determine blast radius
  1. Identify affected services/endpoints and customer impact.
  2. Query recent alerts and graphs: Datadog dashboards, Prometheus metrics (cpu/memory/latency), and request logs.

- Step 2: Quick mitigation options (pick applicable)
  - Redirect traffic to healthy region or model variant.
  - Scale up replicas / add GPU nodes in Dedicated pools. Example: kubectl scale deployment/api --replicas=10 --namespace=prod.
  - Enable cached responses / fallback to cached KV for prefix hits.
  - Apply temporary rate limits or circuit breaker at edge load balancer.
  - Rollback the most recent deployment: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api --namespace=prod --to-revision=<n>.

- Step 3: Deeper investigation
  1. Collect core dumps, logs, and profiler snapshots.
  2. Reproduce with canary traffic or synthetic requests.
  3. Check kernel and GPU logs for OOM/driver errors.

- Step 4: Restore and harden
  1. Apply long-term fix or follow-up change.
  2. Update runbook with learned mitigation if missing.
  3. Close incident once smoke tests pass for 24 hours (for Sev 1).

Runbook template (copy per service)

- Title: <service-name> runbook
- Owner: <team-person> (pager duty role)
- PagerDuty escalation: <escalation policy id>
- Symptoms / alert names: list (e.g., high-5xx-rate, api-latency-p95)
- Impact: who/what is affected
- Hypotheses: common root causes
- Quick mitigations: numbered list of steps with CLI snippets
- Deep diagnostics: commands and dashboard links
- Recovery validation: metrics to monitor and thresholds
- Post-incident actions: checklist

Example short runbook: API gateway high 5xx rate

- Title: api-gateway high-5xx runbook
- Owner: Priya Menon (api-platform)
- Symptoms: Datadog alert api.5xx.rate > 5% for 3m
- Quick mitigations:
  1. Check upstream health: curl -sS https://internal-api-healthy/health || echo 'fail'
  2. Scale gateway: kubectl scale deployment/api-gateway --replicas=6 -n prod
  3. Enable 5xx circuit breaker on edge: curl -X POST https://ops-api/edge/circuit -d '{"path":"/v1/generate","action":"open"}'
  4. If rollback needed: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway -n prod
- Recovery validation: api.5xx.rate < 0.5% for 10m and synthetic latency p95 < 400ms

Postmortem template and process

- Timeline (chronological)
- Summary (one-paragraph impact statement)
- Root cause (technical summary)
- Contributing factors (process/tools/etc.)
- Corrective actions (owner + due date)
- Follow-up tasks and mitigations planned
- Lessons learned and preventive measures

Process: initial draft within 72 hours, public/internal distribution after review (within 7 days), and action item tracking until closure. Link the postmortem to the incident ticket and to the on-call calendar for retro discussion.

On-call rotations and handoffs

- Rotation length: 1 week primary rotation with weekly backups; Secondary is a 2-week rotation. Exceptions for holidays must be scheduled at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Handoffs: outgoing on-call must provide a 30-minute overlap on Mondays for knowledge transfer and active incidents. Handoff checklist:
  - Current active incidents and status
  - Outstanding action items and owners
  - Recent deploys and risky changes (last 24-48h)
  - Access and credentials checks

- Timezones: schedule fairness across NA/EU/APAC; avoid repeated night shifts for engineers in the same region when possible.

Game days and runbook validation

Purpose: exercise incident response, validate runbooks, measure mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR), and train ICs.

Game day cadence and template:
- Quarterly game days per major subsystems (serving runtime, control plane, networking).
- Pre-game checklist: define scenario, participants, monitoring toggles, rollback plan, and safety kill-switch.
- During game: record time to detection, time to mitigation, and communication quality.
- Post-game: publish play-by-play, update runbooks, and add actions to backlog.

Status page and customer comms templates

Guidelines: be timely, transparent, and avoid speculation. Use plain language, impact, and expected next update. Keep templates short and fill placeholders. Communications Lead must approve external messaging for Sev 1 and Sev 2 incidents.

Template: Short status page update (initial)
- Title: Service degradation affecting text generation API
- Summary: We are currently investigating elevated error rates and increased latency for the text-generation API that may affect some customers.
- Impact: Some requests may return 5xx errors or be delayed. A subset of customers in us-west may be affected.
- Mitigation in progress: Traffic is being routed to healthy replicas; we are rolling back the last deployment for the API gateway.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or when root cause identified.

Template: Customer email (for affected customers)

Subject: Incident update — Text generation API degraded (Redwood Inference)\n\nHi <CustomerContact>,\n\nWe wanted to inform you that between <start_time> and <end_time> some requests to the text generation API experienced increased latency and 5xx errors. Our team identified and mitigated the issue by <mitigation_action>.\n\nImpact: <summary of customer-visible impact>\n\nWhat we did: <short mitigation steps>\n\nNext steps: <postmortem link when available>\n\nIf you experienced data loss or continue to see issues, reply to this thread or reach out to support@redwoodinference.example.com.\n\nThank you for your patience,\nThe Redwood Inference Reliability Team

Post-incident metrics and KPIs

Collect and publish the following for every Sev 1/2 incident:
- MTTA (mean time to acknowledge)
- MTTR (mean time to restore)
- Customer-facing downtime (minutes)
- Number of customers impacted
- Number of rollbacks or emergency changes
- Action item closure rate (target 100% within 90 days)

Operational tooling and links (examples)

- PagerDuty: escalation policy "RI-Prod-Sev1" (link to policy)
- Slack: #incidents, #sre-ops (use incident channel per incident)
- Monitoring: Datadog dashboards (api-latency, serving-runtime-health), Prometheus endpoints (node, exporter), and SLO dashboards
- Incident tracker: Jira project KEY=INCIDENTS; use component tag = <service-name>

Templates and quick references (copyable)

- Create incident channel: /incident create "<short name>" --severity=sev1 --owner=@<ic>
- PagerDuty acknowledgement message: "@pagerduty acknowledged — IC=@<ic>, Severity=<sev>. Initial hypothesis: <short note>"
- Status-page initial post (copy/paste):
  Title: <service> currently experiencing degraded performance\  Body: We are investigating increased error rates affecting <service>. Impacted customers: <customers>. Mitigation in progress: <actions>. Next update: <time>.

Appendix: escalation matrix (example)

- 0–15 minutes: Primary on-call handles incident.
- 15–30 minutes: If no progress, escalate to Secondary.
- 30–60 minutes: IC and Eng Manager notified.
- 60+ minutes: Exec oncall and Customer Success engaged for customer comms.
